summary: Repeated SettingsSync verification retains certificate resources while Settings polling continues.

judgment.rationale: Repeated SettingsSync verification retains certificate resources while Settings polling continues. Hypothesis: repeated signer verification leaves finalizable certificates/chain elements alive and continued page polling amplifies retention, especially with a blocked finalizer. This is an initial investigation direction, not a runtime-confirmed diagnosis.
evidence: Reporter measures about 15 handles/s in Event/Key/WaitCompletionPacket and supplies a redacted ZIP; ending Settings stops growth.
Latest analysis identifies page polling, certificate lifetime and a blocked finalizer, but its predicted page-visit-only trigger is explicitly unverified.
This differs from #51448 Token/Event/Thread growth; interaction through delayed finalization does not make them duplicates.

proposed_fixes.title: Repeated SettingsSync verification retains certificate resources while Settings polling continues
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: repeated signer verification leaves finalizable certificates/chain elements alive and continued page polling amplifies retention, especially with a blocked finalizer.
plan: Audit/dispose owned signed-file and chain-element certificates without disposing objects returned to callers.
Verify polling cancellation/restart when the MWB page unloads/reloads, accounting for reused view models.
Measure verification handle growth with normal and deliberately delayed finalization; preserve all trust/peer checks.
verification: Repeated successful and failed verification leaves certificate-store handles bounded.
Leaving/reopening the page stops/restarts polling correctly and peer verification remains enforced.
